julia-support: Heads up — acme-inc is seeing gateway 5xx/timeouts during a controlled burst test hitting /v1/generate. ~30% 503/504s for a ~200 concurrent connections workload. Customer key: acme-inc-org-42.

julia-support: Sample log snippets:
```
2024-11-27T03:23:10Z inference-gateway ERROR request_id=rq_abc123 upstream_read_timeout 504
2024-11-27T03:23:11Z proxy WARN request_id=rq_abc123 response=503 service_unavailable
2024-11-27T03:23:12Z inference-gateway ERROR request_id=rq_def456 connection refused to model-pod
```

mike-sre: Thx. Can you drop a few request_ids and the prometheus CPU/memory spikes for that window? Any deploys or config changes around 03:20-03:25?

julia-support: Request IDs: rq_abc123, rq_def456, rq_gh789. There was a tenant-scoped deploy ~03:22 (model-serving:v2.3). Prom graphs show node CPU spike ~+60% and ready pod count stayed low for ~30s while queue built up. Screenshot: https://redwood.internal/graphs/acme-burst (internal).

devops-bot: Deploy event: model-serving:v2.3 rolled at 2024-11-27T03:22:15Z by ci-cd-bot. ScaledObject acme-pool last patch: cooldownPeriod=300s pollingInterval=30s minReplicaCount=0.

sara-ops: Sounds like KEDA didn't react fast enough. Check ScaledObject annotations: pollingInterval and cooldownPeriod. If pollingInterval=30s and minReplicaCount=0, bursts can hit an empty pool. Also check HPA targetUtilization vs observed metrics.

alex-eng: Also look at model-init readinessProbe — if the model container is doing a model fetch + warmup (quantize/compile) it can take 20-45s, pod stays NotReady, and the autoscaler counts fewer ready pods. We saw model registry latency earlier. Consider prewarming or initialReplicas>0 for heavy tenants.

ben-platform: Quick mitigation: set minReplicaCount=1 for that ScaledObject or reduce pollingInterval to 15s. We can also route to a lighter quantized variant as fallback. Example patch: `kubectl patch scaledobject acme-pool -p '{"spec":{"minReplicaCount":1}}' --type=merge`

phil-support: Note: there was a short billing/auth outage at 03:21 which caused retries from clients — that amplified the burst. We saw some 401/403s earlier that rapidly recovered. Might be correlated.

mike-sre: Agreed. Action items: 1) increase minReplicaCount=1 for acme-pool (apply now), 2) set pollingInterval=15s, 3) add a warmup job to pre-cache model weights on nodes for tenant bursts, 4) follow up with billing team about the 03:21 blip. I'll take 1+2 now. :thumbsup:

julia-support: Patch applied: minReplicaCount=1, pollingInterval=15. Watching metrics now and notified acme oncall (oncall@acme).

devops-bot: Kubernetes event: ScaledObject acme-pool scaled to 3 replicas at 2024-11-27T03:25:40Z.

julia-support: Quick follow-up: error rate dropped from ~30% to ~1% within 2 minutes of scaling. Customer temporarily satisfied, wants RCA and long-term fix (prewarm or reserved capacity).

mike-sre: Notes for RCA: capture model-init container logs, measure model fetch times from registry, check KEDA metric server latency, and evaluate setting initialReplicas>0 or scheduled prewarm for known bursty tenants. Reopen incident if errors reappear.

julia-support: Marking this thread for eng-runtime follow-up and filing post-incident ticket. Will update once RCA is complete.
